events.summary:
A slow moving weather system will continue to impact the region
through Sunday. The risk of flooding continues, especially over
Southeast Montana and Northeast Wyoming.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible, along
with flash flooding over recent burn scars.

* WHERE...All of South Central and Southeast Montana, and Sheridan
County Wyoming.

* WHEN...Through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks and
other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in
poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The heaviest rainfall is slowly shifting over Southeastern
Montana and Northeast Wyoming. The risk of flooding over
south-centeral Montana is decreasing.
- The Robertson Draw, East Side, Elk, and McGhee-Remington burn
scars are particularly vulnerable to Flash Flooding and debris
flows. Any other burn scars from this summer will have elevated
Flash Flood potential as well.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Yap State with a few areas of stronger
gusts north of Faraulep.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. By
midweek, models indicate the potential for a circulation to slowly
organize as it passes between Yap and Guam into the Philippine Sea.
As this happens, westerly winds and gusts will increase with showers
and thunderstorms. While these conditions will generally be felt
across Yap State, portions of the Republic of Palau could see heavy
showers and thunderstorms dropping south early in the week.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.
